summary: A 1934 steel-tower lookout lost its cab in the 1959 Morton fire and was rebuilt in 1960; volunteers staff it when they can, and visits are allowed only when someone is on duty.

facts.design: 14x14-ft CL-100 metal cab (rebuilt 1960) on the existing steel tower

access.note: Volunteer-staffed; drive-up and cab visits only when staffed; no overnight stays. The 2025 Mountains Foundation page reported a Line Fire closure order, which the Forest Service page updated May 11, 2026 does not mention.

visit.trail_note: Narrow dirt road FS 1N12 off Hwy 38; high clearance recommended; gate about 1.5 miles up, summit about 1.5 miles past it. If unstaffed, park at the gate.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, San Bernardino National Forest

events.note: Lookout built on a steel tower; NHLR and Mountains Foundation both give 1934. The first cab was wooden.
Cab destroyed by the Morton fire of July 24, 1959; lookout Aleta (one report: Aletha) Johnson rescued by helicopter.
New steel cab on the existing steel tower; contract let May 1960; lookout moved in by August 1, 1960. NHLR says 1960; Mountains Foundation says 1961.
Described as a lookout tower staffed by the U.S. Forest Service.
Vandals set off a bomb in the tower's garage; the tower was reported slated for a move to the Toiyabe National Forest. Later sources place it still on Morton Peak.
Restored by volunteers and returned to active service; Mountains Foundation says refurbished in 2001.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 27, 2006.
Kept open all year because of high fire danger; the report planned to return the site to a rental system in 2015.

corrections.proposed: remove (no source gives a tower height)
corrections.why: None of the sources read give a tower height. 152.4 m (500 ft) is unsupported and looks wrong for a lookout with a 14x14 cab.

corrections.proposed: 1960 (cab rebuilt; lookout moved in by August 1960)
corrections.why: NHLR says the tower was rebuilt in 1960, and newspapers report the contract in May 1960 and occupancy by August 1960. The Mountains Foundation's 1961 date is recorded as a conflict.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and 1960 newspaper reports point to 1960. The Mountains Foundation says 1961, and a January 1961 annual summary describes the new tower as constructed. Recorded as 1960 with the 1961 date noted.
A July 1959 report spells the name Aletha Johnson; an August 1959 report and the Mountains Foundation use Aleta. Kept as Aleta with the variant noted.
A 1992 report said the tower was slated to move to the Toiyabe National Forest. NHLR (2001 restoration on site) and the Forest Service page place it on Morton Peak. Recorded as still on site.

The Mountains Foundation (2025 season) says the area was closed under a Line Fire closure order. The Forest Service page updated May 11, 2026 does not mention a closure. Unresolved; check before a visit.
NHLR gives 4,593 ft (1,400 m), matching the brief. The Mountains Foundation gives 4,624 ft. Kept NHLR's value.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 152.4 is unsupported; no source gives a tower height, so it is proposed for removal. Brief's 1961 rebuild date is corrected to 1960 on NHLR and newspaper evidence, with the Mountains Foundation's 1961 noted. Current status conflicts: the Mountains Foundation (2025) says closed under a Line Fire closure order, while the Forest Service page (updated May 11, 2026) gives drive-up and cab-visit rules when staffed and mentions no closure. A search snippet described the Forest Service page as closed and last updated March 2025; the fetched page says May 11, 2026, so the story uses the fetched text. The 2014 report's planned 2015 rental system is not confirmed by any later source read. Staffing as of 2026 is from the Forest Service page and NHLR, not a dated roster.
